newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland passes bill approving Telecom share sale.
newsitem.headline: Ireland passes bill approving Telecom share sale.

text.p: The Irish parliament on Wednesday approved a bill to allow the sale of shares in the state-owned telecommunications company, Telecom Eireann, to the Dutch-Swedish consortium KPN-Telia.

KPN-Telia will pay an initial 183 million punts for 20 percent of the shares in Telecom. In addition, it will pay 200 million punts over the next three years for a further 15 percent, bringing its total stake to 35 percent.
Under a profit-sharing deal, KPN-Telia will pay more to the government, provided Telecom increases its profits in future years.
Minister of State Emmet Stagg told parliament that this should bring the state a total of over 500 million punts for the 35 per cent stake in Telecom Eireann.
